A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MVU research. Their main text, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: V2 reports original MVU and modality-constrained baseline evaluations on EgoSchema, NExT-QA, robotics datasets, ActivityNet-QA, and Something-Something-v2, including component ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains these original experiments and adds LVNet-based evaluations, LongVideoBench results, and further analyses of frame counts, context usage, and multi-frame LLaVA.

M1.justification: The object-information extraction, language fusion, likelihood-selection equations, and prompt templates remain unchanged. However, v2 Figure 3 and Appendix B explicitly attribute frame selection to the VLM, while v3 removes that attribution. Equation (1) already specifies a center frame in both versions. The PDFs therefore leave unclear whether a selection component was removed or inconsistent documentation was corrected; the new backbone integrations do not resolve this.

E1.justification: V3 adds LongVideoBench evaluation for videos longer than those emphasized in the existing benchmarks (Appendix H). EgoSchema, NExT-QA, ActivityNet-QA, Open X-Embodiment, and Something-Something-v2 coverage is retained. This extends the existing video-QA coverage rather than introducing the previously reported robotics or motion tasks anew.

E2.justification: Tables 2–3 substantially expand the comparisons with methods including InternVideo2, Tarsier, LangRepo, LifelongMemory, MoreVQA, VideoAgent, VideoTree, LVNet, and ViperGPT. V3 also adds the GPT-4 LLoVi variant to NExT-QA comparisons and a multi-frame LLaVA comparison in Appendix L. ShortViViT and CaKE-LM with HGA disappear from their respective tables; v3's generic CaKE-LM row retains the v2 CoMem results.

E3.justification: V3 introduces LVNet-based and Phi-3-Vision-Instruct evaluation configurations, MVU frame-count settings up to 128 frames, multi-frame LLaVA settings, and average input-token measurements. These substantially extend the evaluation design. Table 2 also revises the stated EgoSchema test-set size from 8564 to 5031; because v2 Appendix B already describes a 5000-plus-video set, this correction does not establish resampling or rerunning.

E4.justification: V3 adds analyses testing MVU's accuracy and runtime as frame counts increase, its token consumption relative to LLoVi, and whether directly supplying multiple frames to LLaVA helps (Tables A.9–A.11). Appendix F.2 adds a semantic-matching toy experiment. The original component, likelihood-selection, frame-description, and motion ablations remain; Table A.5 explicitly redisplays existing Table 6 results rather than adding an experiment.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. V3's additional accuracy, timing, and token-count results do not introduce uncertainty estimation or a different statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: The original 13B MVU results remain, including 37.6 on EgoSchema, 55.4 on NExT-QA, and 42.2 on ActivityNet-QA. V3 newly reports LVNet+MVU at 61.3 and 73.3 versus LVNet's 61.1 and 72.9, and Phi-3+MVU at 50.4 versus 49.7 on LongVideoBench. These are additional configurations, not improvements over v2 under identical settings. New analyses report frame-scaling trends and 1124 versus 1940 average tokens for MVU versus LLoVi. Several EgoSchema subset comparison scores and Just-LLM's full-set result are removed.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, object representations, fusion equation, and likelihood/cross-entropy derivation in Equations (1)–(5) are retained. Appendix F.2 adds an intuitive semantic explanation and empirical example, without introducing a new formal assumption, theorem, proof, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the central claims about modality-constrained performance, efficient likelihood selection, and MVU generality. The introduction qualifies the baseline contribution from 'no access' to 'limited access' to video-specific information and replaces prospective backbone compatibility with an explicit claim of demonstrated integration and improvements across 20 datasets. These refine the retained contributions.

C2.justification: V3 substantially extends the mechanism explanations: Appendix K interprets object-centric extraction as an information bottleneck that filters irrelevant and repetitive information and can complement frame selection. Appendix F.2 argues that likelihood selection captures semantic compatibility beyond exact matching. Appendices H and L additionally discuss compute constraints and why naive multi-frame input can fail. V2's world-knowledge and robotics-domain interpretations remain.

D1.justification: V3 supplies an MVU repository address in the abstract and an LVNet code source in the reproducibility statement. It also clarifies common-model baseline comparisons and provides explicit batched prompting examples. Most existing model identifiers, hardware, extraction settings, and templates remain unchanged. The supplied PDFs establish these access instructions, not the repositories' actual availability.

R1.justification: V3 updates the research context with newer video-QA methods and the LongVideoBench/Phi-3 references. It acknowledges Min et al.'s similar modality-constrained findings and removes zero video-level training from the stated distinction against other zero-shot approaches in Section 2. These are focused updates to the existing related-work organization and novelty positioning.

P1.justification: The main section organization and much of the prose remain intact. V3 locally rewrites the contribution summary, likelihood-selection explanation, and benchmark discussion, expands appendix explanations, and adds author contributions, acknowledgments, and conference headers. Existing appendix material is retained despite renumbering.

P2.justification: Table 2 is substantially reorganized: frame-count and subset columns disappear, a closed-model column appears, and comparison groups expand. Table 3 expands and changes its category headings from Causal/Why/How to Cau./Tem./Des. Table 1 gains frame counts, Figure 3's labeling changes, and Figure 4 moves relative to Table 4. The appendix adds several displays, including the repeated ablation in Table A.5 and new Tables A.7 and A.9–A.11.

improvement.justification: V3 improves empirical support through additional backbone and longer-video evaluations, frame-scaling controls, and measured token efficiency, while clarifying prompting and providing code access information. The gains are tempered by removed subset comparisons, unresolved implementation ambiguity, and absent uncertainty reporting. Its state-of-the-art wording also remains insufficiently qualified: newly included LifelongMemory exceeds LVNet+MVU on EgoSchema (62.4 versus 61.3), and VideoTree exceeds it on NExT-QA (73.5 versus 73.3). The net improvement is useful but limited.
